title: IBKR portfolio import: use the real buy date from IBKR trade/execution history as entry_date, if possible
description:
User-requested, explicitly framed as 'if possible' -- this is a genuine research task, not a pre-diagnosed fix. Confirmed via reading the current code before writing this task: `entry_date` for every position imported via `POST /api/ibkr/portfolio-preload` is unconditionally `today()` (backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py ~line 687), with an explanatory note template (`_IBKR_IMPORT_ENTRY_NOTE_TEMPLATE`, ~lines 506-517) that already says why: 'IBKR's positions endpoint does not report when a position was opened.' This was a deliberate, already-reasoned limitation of the SPECIFIC IBKR endpoint this app currently calls for positions (`GET /iserver/accounts`'s position data, via `IBKRProvider.get_account_positions()`, backend/app/data/ibkr_provider.py ~line 1031) -- not an oversight, and that endpoint genuinely has no per-position open-date field to read.

IBKR's Client Portal Web API separately exposes trade/execution-history endpoints that DO carry per-execution dates -- e.g. `GET /iserver/account/trades` (recent executions) and the Portfolio Analyst `/pa/transactions` endpoint (potentially deeper history). Confirmed via grep that neither has been investigated or used anywhere in this codebase: `IBKRProvider` currently has no method touching either path, and `docs/ideas.md` has no existing research note about them (unlike `/iserver/marketdata/history`/`/iserver/scanner/*`, which this codebase's prior IBKR tasks already researched and documented before building against them -- see `docs/tasks/done/backend-ibkr-*.json` for that research style/precedent to follow here). Whether either endpoint is actually reachable through this app's existing gateway session/auth flow, for this account type (paper vs. live), with usable rate limits, is genuinely unknown going in.

checklist.step: Research IBKR's Client Portal Web API for an endpoint that returns per-position trade/execution history with dates for the currently-authenticated account -- candidates named above, `/iserver/account/trades` and `/pa/transactions`. Confirm which (if any) is actually reachable through `IBKRProvider`'s existing `_request`/`_require_available` gateway-session machinery before assuming either works, the same way prior IBKR tasks confirmed their own endpoint's real behavior before building against it.

If a usable endpoint exists: decide and record what 'entry date' should mean when a position was built from multiple historical buy executions at different dates/prices -- the earliest buy date, the most recent ('last buy date', the user's own phrasing), or something else -- checking this against the existing precedent in `PositionIn.entry_date`'s own documented same-ticker-merge rule ('the earlier of the two entry dates is kept', schemas.py) for consistency, rather than inventing an unrelated convention.

If genuinely not possible (endpoint inaccessible, no historical data available for this account type, or data too unreliable to trust for this purpose): record that finding and the reasoning as a `decisions` entry and close this task with no code change -- an investigated, well-reasoned 'not currently possible' is a valid, complete outcome for an explicitly 'if possible' task.

If possible: implement, and update `_IBKR_IMPORT_ENTRY_NOTE_TEMPLATE`'s wording so it reflects the new actual behavior (a real date when available, with a clear note for whichever position(s) still fall back to today's date, rather than the current blanket claim that this is never possible).
Tests covering both the success path (mocking the new endpoint call) and the fallback-to-`today()` path for a position the new endpoint can't explain.

Update `IBKRPortfolioPreloadImportedPositionOut.entry_date`'s own schema description (and `docs/architecture/API.md` if its documented contract changes) if behavior changes, then run `python scripts/export_openapi.py` from `backend/` and commit the regenerated `backend/openapi.json` per CLAUDE.md's API documentation standard.

decisions.decision:
Investigated both named candidate endpoints (`GET /iserver/account/trades`, `POST /pa/transactions`) against IBKR's own documented Client Portal Web API behavior and this session's actual (limited) live-reachability check, and concluded: NOT CURRENTLY POSSIBLE to use either as a trustworthy source for `entry_date` on `POST /api/ibkr/portfolio-preload`. No code change made; `_IBKR_IMPORT_ENTRY_NOTE_TEMPLATE`/`entry_date`/`IBKRPortfolioPreloadImportedPositionOut.entry_date` are left exactly as-is.

Live-reachability attempt (be precise about what this does and doesn't show): this session ran `IBKRProvider(base_url='https://ibkr.home.arpa/v1/api').get_gateway_status()` (the base URL this devcontainer's own `backend/.env` is already configured with) and got `GatewayStatus(state='gateway_unreachable', detail='IBKR gateway returned HTTP 401 from /iserver/auth/status')`. That 401 is NOT treated as evidence either way about a real gateway's auth state: `curl -v` against the same URL returned response headers (`server-timing: ak_p`, `cdn-cache: MISS`, Akamai-edge-style framing) that are inconsistent with a direct connection terminating at `ibkr.home.arpa`'s resolved address (`192.168.10.40`, an RFC1918 private LAN address -- `getent hosts` resolved it, but a cloud dev sandbox has no real network path to a private home-LAN address, so completing a TLS handshake and getting a structured HTTP response from it at all is itself the tell that something in this environment's own egress path intercepted the request before it ever reached a real IBKR gateway). Hitting the same IP directly by address (bypassing the hostname/SNI) returned a bare `404` with none of those headers, reinforcing that the two paths are hitting different things, not the same backend. Net effect: this session could not get a live, authenticated answer from a real IBKR gateway for ANY endpoint (old or new), consistent with this task's own framing that live access 'may or may not be reachable' here, and with `backend-ibkr-portfolio-preload`/`backend-ibkr-conid-db-cache` etc.'s own prior-recorded no-live-gateway research pattern for this exact module. No claim of live verification, positive or negative, is made beyond that.

Documented-behavior research (this is the actual basis for the 'not possible' conclusion, independent of the live-reachability gap above): `GET /iserver/account/trades` is IBKR's own documented 'recent executions' endpoint, scoped to the current day plus the six previous calendar days only -- there is no parameter to page or widen that window further back. `POST /pa/transactions` (Portfolio Analyst) goes deeper but is still a bounded, parameterized date-range/day-count lookback, not an unbounded full-history query, and Portfolio Analyst data additionally depends on the connected account actually having PA entitlement active -- not guaranteed for every IBKR account tier, and genuinely unknown for whichever account any real deployment of this app would connect to (paper vs. live, exactly the open unknown this task's own description already flagged). Both of these are real, structural properties of IBKR's documented API surface, not merely 'unverified against a live gateway' -- they would hold regardless of whether this session could reach a live gateway or not.

Why that sinks the feature even setting reachability aside: `POST /api/ibkr/portfolio-preload`'s whole premise is importing an account's EXISTING, already-held positions -- by far the common case for a position someone wants to bulk-import is one opened well before any ~7-day (or even a longer-but-still-bounded PA) lookback window, not within it. For such a position, neither candidate endpoint returns anything to match at all -- exactly the same 'nothing to work with' outcome as today's unconditional `today()` fallback, buying nothing. Worse, for a position whose ONLY execution activity inside the lookback window is a partial top-up/add (common: scaling into an existing long-held position), both endpoints WOULD return a real, resolvable execution date -- just the wrong one: the add date, not the position's true original entry date. Code built against either endpoint has no way to tell 'this position's full history fits inside the window' apart from 'this position is older than the window and I'm only seeing a partial add' without already knowing the true entry date it's trying to determine. That would produce a confidently-wrong-looking real date for exactly the positions a trader is most likely to have held for a while and most likely to trust the new field for -- strictly worse than the current honest 'today's date, with an explicit note that it's not the real purchase date' fallback, which is precisely the harm `_IBKR_IMPORT_ENTRY_NOTE_TEMPLATE`'s existing comment was written to avoid ('misleading... feeding a wrong trade-duration/entry-timing read'). This satisfies this task's own checklist item 3 bar for a valid 'not possible' outcome ('data too unreliable to trust for this purpose'), independent of the live-reachability gap.

Checklist item 2's question (what 'entry date' should mean for a position built from multiple buy executions) was still worth settling in principle, for whoever revisits this if IBKR ever exposes deeper, genuinely unbounded transaction history: the earliest buy execution date, matching `PositionIn.entry_date`'s own documented same-ticker-merge rule ('the earlier of the two entry dates is kept', `backend/app/api/schemas.py`) for consistency -- not the most recent/'last buy date', which would also be the WORSE of the two conventions for the exact partial-top-up failure mode above (it's the one most likely to look like a confident answer while actually being the add date, not the original entry).

Revisit this if: (a) a real deployment confirms (against an actually-reachable, authenticated gateway, which this session could not do) that `pa/transactions` is enabled for that specific account AND reaches back further than any position this app would realistically import, or (b) IBKR ever documents a genuinely unbounded transaction-history endpoint. Neither holds today.
decisions.rationale: The task explicitly frames an investigated, well-reasoned 'not currently possible' as a valid, complete outcome for an 'if possible' research task (checklist item 3) -- forcing an implementation against an endpoint whose own documented scope structurally can't support the feature's actual requirement (arbitrary-age existing positions, not just recently-opened ones) would trade an honest, already-explained `today()` fallback for a worse one that looks precise but is silently wrong for exactly the positions most likely to need it. Rejected alternative: implement against `/iserver/account/trades` anyway and only use it when a matching execution happens to fall inside the lookback window, falling back to `today()` otherwise (literally what checklist item 4 describes as the 'if possible' shape) -- rejected specifically because of the partial-top-up failure mode above: this session has no way to distinguish (within that implementation) 'genuinely opened inside the window' from 'held longer than the window, this is just a later add,' so shipping it would silently mislabel the second case as the first for any position with in-window top-up activity, which is a materially worse and harder-to-notice failure than the current, already-labeled `today()` fallback. Chose to record this as a decisions entry rather than a questions entry because nothing here is a product call only the user can make -- it's a technical research conclusion the worker is positioned to reach and justify itself, per CLAUDE.md's decisions-vs-questions distinction.

decisions.decision:
SUPERSEDES the prior round's central impossibility claim, per `pr-reviewer`'s PR #408 blocking finding: the claim that code has 'no way to tell a genuinely-new in-window position apart from a partial top-up on an older position without already knowing the true entry date' was wrong, because `IBKRAccountPosition.quantity` (already fetched independently of any trade data) gives the currently-held quantity, and that CAN be reconciled against the trades-window's own net buy/sell quantity to distinguish the two cases. Implemented the reconciliation-gated subset, exactly as the review requested (option a): `IBKRProvider.get_account_trades()` (new method, `GET /iserver/account/trades`, `backend/app/data/ibkr_provider.py`) fetches recent executions (a new `IBKRTrade` dataclass + `_parse_account_trades`/`_parse_trade_side`/`_parse_trade_date` parsing helpers, following the established `_request`/`_require_available`/dataclass-plus-parse-function pattern `get_account_positions`/`IBKRAccountPosition`/`_parse_account_positions` already use). `app/api/routers/ibkr.py`'s new `_derive_entry_date(position, trades, fallback)` reconciles per-conid: if `trades` contains buy(s) for this conid whose net-of-sells quantity exactly matches (`math.isclose`, `abs_tol=1e-6`) the position's currently-held `quantity`, the EARLIEST matching buy date is returned as a real `entry_date` (matching `PositionIn.entry_date`'s documented same-ticker-merge 'earlier date wins' convention, per checklist item 2's original research) -- otherwise (no in-window activity for this conid, or only a partial/top-up match) it falls back to `today()`, byte-identical to this feature's pre-existing behavior. `preload_ibkr_portfolio` calls `get_account_trades()` once per request and catches `IBKRUnavailableError` around it specifically (distinct from the existing positions-fetch try/except, which still returns 503) -- a trades-endpoint failure degrades every candidate in the batch to the fallback branch rather than breaking the import, per the review's explicit requirement. `_IBKR_IMPORT_ENTRY_NOTE_TEMPLATE` is now two templates (`_IBKR_IMPORT_ENTRY_NOTE_DERIVED_TEMPLATE`/`_IBKR_IMPORT_ENTRY_NOTE_FALLBACK_TEMPLATE`) chosen per position by `_derive_entry_date`'s own `derived` flag, since which case applied now genuinely varies within the same import call. `IBKRPortfolioPreloadImportedPositionOut.entry_date`'s schema description and `docs/architecture/API.md`'s `POST /api/ibkr/portfolio-preload` section were both rewritten to describe the new per-position behavior instead of the old blanket 'always today()' claim; `backend/openapi.json` regenerated via `scripts/export_openapi.py` and committed. New tests: `tests/unit/data/test_ibkr_provider.py`'s `TestGetAccountTrades` (parsing: B/S and spelled-out BUY/SELL sides, non-string/unrecognized side dropped, trade_time_r-preferred-over-trade_time date parsing with both falling back correctly including an OverflowError-on-absurd-epoch case, per-account filtering including the no-account-field-kept case, non-positive-quantity/non-dict-row/missing-conid/unparseable-date all dropped) and `tests/integration/test_ibkr_portfolio_preload.py`'s new cases under `TestPreloadIbkrPortfolio` (exact-match derives a real date, multiple buys pick the earliest, net-of-sells reconciliation still derives correctly, a partial top-up falls back, no trade history for this conid falls back, and the trades-endpoint-unavailable case falls back without breaking the 200/available response) -- full backend suite re-run clean, ruff/mypy clean, coverage 99.95% (gate 90%).

Being honest about what this round did and didn't verify (same constraint the prior round and PR #408's review both already flagged): there is still no live, authenticated IBKR gateway reachable from this sandbox to test the real `GET /iserver/account/trades` response shape against -- this implementation, like every other method in `IBKRProvider`, is built and tested entirely against IBKR's own documented field shapes (`conid`, `side` as `"B"`/`"S"` per IBKR's documented example, `size`, `account`, `trade_time_r`/`trade_time`), not a captured live response. No claim of live endpoint verification is made here; the basis is documented behavior plus mocked tests, exactly as `pr-reviewer`'s PR #408 comment already characterized the honest basis for this task. The multi-sub-account account-id filtering and the spelled-out-BUY/SELL defensive acceptance are both this session's own conservative choices, not independently confirmed against a live payload, in case a real gateway's actual field values turn out to differ once someone can test against one.

Resolved checklist items 4-6 (left `done=false` with no annotation, per the review's second, non-central finding) to `done=true` now that the implementation, tests, and schema/OpenAPI update are all complete.
decisions.rationale: `pr-reviewer`'s counterexample is correct and this round's own re-derivation confirms why: for conid C, held_quantity = pre_window_quantity + net_window_quantity (buys minus sells, all in `get_account_trades`'s ~7-day window) -- since every quantity here is non-negative, `net_window_quantity == held_quantity` can only hold when `pre_window_quantity == 0`, i.e. this position's entire history fits inside the window, making the earliest in-window buy date trustworthy. A non-matching case (pre_window_quantity > 0, or a corporate action silently changing held_quantity without a matching trade row) always pushes `net_window_quantity` below `held_quantity`, landing in the conservative fallback branch rather than ever producing a false-positive confident date -- the one way this could still mislead (an exact, coincidental numeric cancellation between an untracked corporate action and in-window trade activity) was evaluated and judged negligible rather than ignored, consistent with the review's own framing of what a sound rejection-on-the-merits would need to look like. Rejected alternative (considered and discarded, not attempted): deriving entry_date even on a partial/top-up match by somehow discounting it -- rejected because there's no way to know the discount amount without the very pre-window history this task is trying to avoid assuming, which is exactly the original 'not possible' round's correct half of the argument (the window being inherently bounded) -- only its 'no way to distinguish the two cases' half was wrong, and this round's fix is narrowly targeted at that specific error rather than relitigating the parts of the original research that `pr-reviewer` independently reconfirmed were accurate (the 7-day/days-param window claims).

decisions.decision: Accepted `pr-decision`'s PR #408 override and implemented its identified fix: `_parse_account_trades` (`backend/app/data/ibkr_provider.py`) now drops a trade row with no `"account"` field at all, instead of keeping it. The filter condition changed from `if isinstance(row_account, str) and row_account and row_account != account_id: continue` (drop only when `account` is present AND differs) to `if not isinstance(row_account, str) or not row_account or row_account != account_id: continue` (drop whenever `account` is missing, non-string, empty, OR different) -- a row now needs a present, non-empty, matching `account` string to be kept at all. Updated both docstrings that documented the old 'kept' behavior (`get_account_trades`'s own docstring and `_parse_account_trades`'s) to describe the new fail-closed behavior and why. Updated the unit test that asserted the old behavior (`test_row_with_no_account_field_is_kept` -> `test_row_with_no_account_field_is_dropped`, `tests/unit/data/test_ibkr_provider.py`), now asserting the row is dropped while a same-batch correctly-attributed row is still kept. No other code, schema, or API-facing behavior needed to change: `openapi.json` was regenerated and diffed byte-identical against the committed snapshot, confirming no route/schema signature changed.
decisions.rationale: `pr-decision`'s argument is correct and is accepted in full, not just implemented under instruction: the quantity-reconciliation guard in `_derive_entry_date` (backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py) is only sound because every possible reconciliation error can be shown to push toward the conservative `today()` fallback, never manufacture a false-positive quantity match -- that's the entire basis the prior round's decisions entry used to justify shipping the feature at all. The corporate-action gap that same prior entry explicitly accepted as negligible satisfies that property (an untracked corporate action can only remove quantity from the trade-visible picture, pushing net_window_quantity further from, not coincidentally onto, a match). A cross-account contaminating row does NOT satisfy that property: unlike an untracked corporate action, a different account's own real buy/sell activity on the same conid, folded in because it happened to omit an `account` field, can add OR subtract quantity in either direction -- meaning it can push an otherwise non-matching net_window_quantity (pre_window_quantity > 0, i.e. truly held longer than the window) exactly up to equal held_quantity, satisfying the isclose guard by coincidence and producing a confidently-wrong derived entry_date instead of the safe fallback. That is a genuine false positive, not just an unverified edge case, and it is precisely the 'confidently wrong is worse than an honest fallback' failure mode this task's own original research invoked when it first argued the feature wasn't safely buildable at all. Fail-closed on a missing `account` field also brings this one field in line with every other field this same function already treats as 'uncertain means drop' (conid/side/quantity/date), rather than leaving it as the sole exception. No alternative was seriously considered beyond the one `pr-decision` already proposed (drop on missing) -- a narrower fix (only drop a missing-account row when a multi-account session is detected) was briefly considered and rejected as unnecessary complexity: single-account sessions are unaffected by dropping unconditionally (every real row in that case already carries the one true account id, matching `_discover_account_id`'s own `selectedAccount`-or-first-account resolution), so there is no real-world case this fix costs anything in, only one it protects against. Note this entry corrects, via CLAUDE.md's append-only convention rather than editing it in place, the prior round's decisions entry above, which had characterized the missing-account-field-kept behavior as an intentional, justified choice ('needlessly destructive for the common case') -- that characterization is now superseded by the argument above.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-verified round-3 commit 9308ffc4: re-ran backend suite (1644 passed, 99.95% coverage, ruff/mypy clean) and re-exported openapi.json (byte-identical, no diff). Confirmed the fix is exactly what my round-2 override asked for by reading the new condition (`not isinstance(row_account, str) or not row_account or row_account != account_id`) and reproducing the mutation test myself: reverted it to the old `and`-based form, re-ran test_row_with_no_account_field_is_dropped, saw it fail ([1, 2] != [2]) exactly as pr-reviewer reported, then reverted cleanly (git diff clean afterward). Checked the test's default `_trade_row(account="DU1")` fixture against the mocked `accounts: ["DU1"]` in every other existing test to confirm the stricter filter doesn't wrongly drop any already-passing legitimate row -- it doesn't, since every other test's account matches. Diffed origin/main...HEAD to confirm overall PR scope (provider+router+schemas+tests+openapi+API.md+generated frontend types+task board, no surprises) and confirmed no human PR comment overrides the automated verdict. Judged the one new non-blocking finding (missing dedicated tests for the empty-string/non-string account sub-cases) as genuinely deferrable, not blocking: unlike the round-2 finding it corrects (a real false-positive-manufacturing path demonstrated against this codebase's own existing multi-account test precedent), this is a test-completeness gap on a one-line boolean condition whose correctness across all five cases I independently re-verified by truth table and mutation test, not an unverified behavior -- appropriately filed to backend-ibkr-import-entry-date-from-trades-followups rather than blocking this round.

comments.summary: Re-review of the reconciliation implementation added in response to the prior needs_work round. Verified the core soundness claim algebraically and by mutation test: held = pre_window_quantity + net_window_quantity (buys minus sells, all non-negative since IBKRAccountPosition.quantity/IBKRTrade.quantity are both guaranteed strictly positive -- short/flat positions are dropped upstream by _parse_account_positions, so the 'quantities always positive' premise the decisions entry rests on genuinely holds). net == held can only happen when pre_window_quantity == 0, so an exact match is a sound signal; a corporate action that changes held without a matching trade row can only ever push a position toward the conservative fallback, never produce a false positive. Confirmed this guard is actually load-bearing, not just a comment, by temporarily deleting the math.isclose check and re-running tests: test_entry_date_falls_back_when_trade_history_only_shows_a_partial_top_up immediately failed (asserted 2026-10-10, mutated code returned 2026-10-07), then reverted. Unknown trade sides are correctly fail-closed (_parse_trade_side returns None for anything but B/S/BUY/SELL, caller drops the row rather than guessing), and the IBKRUnavailableError catch around provider.get_account_trades() is correctly and narrowly scoped -- traced the full call chain (_require_available/_discover_account_id/_request/_parse_account_trades) and confirmed IBKRUnavailableError is the only exception type that path can raise; garbage-shaped-but-valid-JSON payloads are handled by _int_or_none/_float_or_none's own TypeError/ValueError catches and _parse_account_trades's isinstance(payload, list) check, never raising past this method.

Non-blocking: _parse_trade_date converts trade_time_r (epoch ms) via UTC but the trade_time string fallback has no timezone handling at all, and neither is verified against a live IBKR payload (no reachable gateway in this environment). For a regular-hours trade this can't matter, but an extended-hours execution near the UTC day boundary risks a silent off-by-one-day entry_date, and since reconciliation only checks quantity (not date), a date error of this kind wouldn't be caught by the existing guard. Also non-blocking: a trade row missing the "account" field entirely is kept rather than dropped, which could in principle attribute a different sub-account's execution to this account in a multi-sub-account session -- also unverified against a live payload. Both tracked on backend-ibkr-import-entry-date-from-trades-followups rather than only here, since this comment disappears once the PR merges.

pr-decision override: the second 'non-blocking' finding above (missing-"account"-field rows kept, not dropped) is actually blocking, not cosmetic, and should not have been deferred to the followups task. _parse_account_trades's filter (`if isinstance(row_account, str) and row_account and row_account != account_id: continue`) only drops a row when `account` is present AND different -- a row with no `account` field at all is unconditionally kept and attributed to whichever account is running preload. This is not a theoretical multi-account scenario invented for this review: get_account_positions's own existing tests (tests/unit/data/test_ibkr_provider.py:1796, `test_discovers_account_via_selected_account`, payload `{"accounts": ["DU000001", "DU000002"], "selectedAccount": "DU000002"}`) already demonstrate this codebase anticipates genuine multi-account IBKR gateway sessions for the exact same gateway login `get_account_trades` shares. For such a session, a trades row belonging to a DIFFERENT account that happens to omit `account` is silently folded into this account's own conid-level quantity reconciliation in _derive_entry_date (backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py:604-611). Unlike the corporate-action gap the decisions entry (PR #408 round 2) explicitly analyzed and accepted as negligible -- which can only ever push a true match toward the conservative fallback, never manufacture a false positive -- a contaminating row from a different account's trading on the same conid CAN manufacture a false positive: it can add or remove quantity that happens to make an otherwise-non-matching net exactly equal the held quantity, producing a confidently-derived-but-wrong entry_date that passes the isclose guard untouched (the guard only ever sees the post-contamination net, it has no way to tell a cross-account row apart from a legitimate one). That is exactly the 'confidently wrong is worse than an honest fallback' failure mode this task's own original 'not currently possible' research explicitly invoked to argue against building this feature naively -- the quantity-reconciliation fix that unblocked the prior needs_work round closes that failure mode for the single-account case but does not close it for a multi-account session, and the decisions entry's soundness argument doesn't address this path at all. It's also inconsistent with every other ambiguous-field case in the same function, which all default to dropping the row when uncertain (unparseable conid, unrecognized side, non-positive quantity, unparseable date) -- `account` is the one field where 'uncertain' defaults to keep instead of drop, with no comparably rigorous justification. The fix is available without needing live-gateway verification (unlike the timezone finding, which genuinely needs it): drop a row with no `account` field, matching the same conservative-by-default convention the rest of this function already follows, rather than keep it. Re-verified independently: re-ran the full backend suite (1644 passed, 99.95% coverage), ruff/mypy clean, re-ran `python scripts/export_openapi.py` and diffed byte-identical against the committed snapshot, read the full diff (backend/app/data/ibkr_provider.py, backend/app/api/routers/ibkr.py, schemas.py, API.md, both test files), and reproduced the math.isclose mutation test myself (same result pr-reviewer reported) -- all of that holds up. Only this one severity call is being overridden.

Re-review of commit 9308ffc4, which implements pr-decision's override fix. On the record, since I'm the reviewer whose original non-blocking classification was overruled: I now agree with pr-decision's severity call, not just its fix. My round-2 classification of the missing-account-field-kept finding as non-blocking was wrong -- I correctly spotted the behavior but didn't carry the false-positive-vs-safe-fallback analysis (the same one my own round-2 comment above applied to the corporate-action gap) through to this field. pr-decision's distinction holds: a corporate action can only ever subtract untracked quantity, pushing a true non-match further from a coincidental match, while a cross-account row's quantity can move in either direction and so CAN land exactly on a false-positive match. That's a categorical difference in which the account field alone defaulted to 'keep on uncertain' while conid/side/quantity/date all default to 'drop on uncertain' in the same function -- an inconsistency that should have been caught the first time, not just once pointed out. Deferring it to the followups task understated it as the same severity class as the genuinely-deferrable timezone gap. Verifying the fix itself: read the new filter (`not isinstance(row_account, str) or not row_account or row_account != account_id`) and built a truth table over all five cases (missing/empty-string/non-string/different/matching) -- only present-and-matching keeps the row, every other case drops, with no legitimate row wrongly dropped (a matching-string account is the sole keep case, correctly). Mutation-tested the condition by reverting it to the prior form (`isinstance(...) and row_account and row_account != account_id`) and re-running just the renamed test: `test_row_with_no_account_field_is_dropped` failed exactly as expected (`[1, 2] != [2]`), then reverted the file back to the committed version -- confirmed via `git diff --stat` showing no residual change.
